title: Weak point Wednesday: Triceps
summary: NH admits he neglected triceps for his first six years and shares how he is catching up: slingshot and close-grip pressing, high-frequency banded nucleus overload for the lateral and medial heads, a modified skull crusher for the long head and high-rep slingshot half dips. He stresses building a mind-muscle connection and accepting that a neglected part will not catch up in a year.
claims: He barely trained triceps for the first six years of lifting and is now paying for it with catch-up work
A biceps-dominant imbalance is not very injury-prone but can still risk elbow tendon damage and looks unbalanced
The triceps make up most of the arm, so bigger arms require triceps size
Presses alone were never enough to grow his triceps; heavy bench and overhead press did not develop his lateral and medial heads
He does bench strength work with a slingshot to make the lockout relatively harder and protect his damaged shoulder, accepting some lost chest stimulus
Close-grip bench puts more emphasis on the triceps
Nucleus overload for triceps: every two days on non-pressing days, band or cable extensions for 30-40 reps, 4-5 sets, from every angle, focused on lateral and medial heads
If the long head lags, light French presses for the same high reps work
Bands are more forgiving on the tendons than cables, which matters at such high frequency
For the long head, do skull crushers letting the shoulders flex back past vertical so the lats engage; he considers this the superior version
His lateral and medial heads tire out very quickly in compound presses, yet presses alone give poor results for them
Triceps dips: slingshot, half reps, torso as vertical as possible, then lean forward as triceps tire to bring in chest and shoulders; 4 sets of 30, progressing toward 50 reps
In heavy 8-10 rep pressing he loses the triceps connection, so he needs high-rep work where progression speed does not matter
A lagging part needs a conscious connection and different work; doing what you always did will not make it grow
A body part neglected for years will not catch up in one year; newbie gains come quickly but a dominant part stays dominant unless you stop training it
exercises: harder lockout for triceps, protects damaged shoulder
30-40 reps, 4-5 sets, all angles, every 2 days
nucleus overload for lateral/medial heads; easier on tendons than cables
let shoulders flex back past vertical; bar does not come to forehead; engage lats
torso vertical, half reps, lean forward as triceps fatigue; 4x30 toward 50
